chunks: Allah has not made it obligatory on the ignorant to learn till He has made it obligatory on the learned to teach.

key_terms.أَخَذَ عَلَى: made obligatory / took a covenant upon
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَهْلِ: the people of ignorance / the laypeople
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ: the people of knowledge / the scholars

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the obligation of learning in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchical reciprocity in the chain of knowledge, where the scholarly duty to teach is a prerequisite for the layperson's duty to learn. This principle, central to Shia epistemology, underscores that knowledge transmission is a collective obligation (fard kifaya) requiring active dissemination by the learned before it can be effectively received by the ignorant. It highlights the social responsibility of scholars to bridge the gap between divine wisdom and the community.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 478. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Allāh has not made it obligatory on the ignorant to learn till He has made it obligatory on the learned to teach.
